# Aunt Jamesina

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000)</sub>
- **Role:** Housekeeper at Patty's Place  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Aunt Jimsie  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>; Aunty  <sub>[v3 c16 P3](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0003)</sub>

## Appearance

Aunt Jamesina is a tiny old woman with pink cheeks, a little softly triangular face, and large, soft blue eyes. She has snow-white hair which she wears in quaint little puffs over her ears. She dresses in an old-fashioned style.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P3](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0003)_

## Personality

Aunt Jamesina is a cheerful, mirthful, and indulgent woman with a heartful of hopes and youthful spirit. She possesses a philosophy of doing her duty while enjoying life and having a good time. She is outspoken, candid, and often uses humor or sharp wit, yet she harbors deep warmth, kindness, and sympathy for others.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c16 P3](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0003), [v3 c16 P51](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0051), [v3 c19 P4](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0004), [v3 c37 P19](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0019)_

## Traits

- Cheerful and youthful at heart  <sub>[v3 c16 P3](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0003), [v3 c19 P3](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0003)</sub>
- Indulgent and tolerant  <sub>[v3 c16 P3](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0003), [v3 c16 P63](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0063)</sub>
- Horrified by snakes  <sub>[v3 c30 P15](../source/v03-c30.md#nw-v03-c30-p0015), [v3 c38 P15](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0015)</sub>

## Abilities

- Knitting  <sub>[v3 c16 P3](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0003)</sub>
- Housekeeping and managing cats  <sub>[v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c38 P1](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0001)</sub>

## Goals

- To keep house for the girls at Patty's Place and provide a home for them  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c38 P1](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0001)</sub>

## History

Aunt Jamesina agreed to move to Kingsport and act as housekeeper for her niece Stella, along with Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, and Philippa Gordon at Patty's Place. During their college years at Redmond, she provided a warm, motherly home for the girls while letting them live independently. She cared deeply for the house's three cats—Joseph, the Sarah-cat, and Rusty—and chose to remain in Kingsport during holiday breaks to look after them. After the girls graduated from Redmond, she decided to take the three cats to her own home to live with her.

_Sources: [v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c16 P3](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0003), [v3 c16 P56](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0056), [v3 c18 P1](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0001), [v3 c35 P8](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0008), [v3 c37 P29](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0029)_

## Background by volume

- Her father was drowned at sea a month before she was born, so she was named Jamesina after him  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>
- Her husband and mother refused to let her wear a yellow silk dress in her youth  <sub>[v3 c19 P6](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0006)</sub>
- Her daughter married and went to the foreign mission field in India  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c30 P15](../source/v03-c30.md#nw-v03-c30-p0015), [v3 c38 P15](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0015)</sub>

## Quotes

> Do your duty by God and your neighbor and yourself, and have a good time. That's my philosophy and it's always worked pretty well.  <sub>[v3 c19 P4](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0004)</sub>

> When you get rheumatism in your soul you might as well go and pick out your coffin.  <sub>[v3 c25 P10](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0010)</sub>

> When you've learned to laugh at the things that should be laughed at, and not to laugh at those that shouldn't, you've got wisdom and understanding.  <sub>[v3 c37 P20](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0020)</sub>

> Any one who has gumption knows what it is, and any one who hasn't can never know what it is.  <sub>[v3 c37 P28](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0028)</sub>
